text:
maria: noticing a weird pattern this morning — a bunch of small GPU jobs (1-2g) got scattered across racks and then started evicting after NVLink heat spikes. top-level guess: topologySpreadConstraints + late-binding is creating fractional gang placements and cross-rack placement is killing perf

kai: can you paste a couple of pod specs and the scheduler events?

maria: here’s one pod's events:
```
Events:
  Normal Scheduled  10s  kube-scheduler  Successfully assigned default/conv-batch-42 to node-usw2-rack-7-gpu-03
  Warning  FailedScheduling  9s  kube-scheduler  Preempted by higher priority pod
  Normal Pulled  7s  kubelet  Container image pulled
  Warning  Evicted  5s  kubelet  Node resource pressure on nvidia.com/gpu-vram
```

nora: also saw network counters spike between those racks around same time: tx qdepth on the host NIC jumped 3x, we had packet drops on the nvlink-enabled hosts 

kai: hmm — fractional gang scheduling + topologySpread could cause a single logical job to be split across NVLink islands. When KV cache warms, we get cross-host traffic. That plus local VRAM pressure = OOM/evicts.

sam: logs from the allocator show many small allocations preferring 'spread' policy: "alloc_strategy=topologySpread;preferLateBind=true;packThreshold=0.6"

leah: metric I created: fractional_gang_ratio = fraction of pods in a job that are not colocated on same NVLink island. Yesterday peaked at 0.78 during the incident window.

maria: proposal: add a scheduler plugin to prefer co-location for pods with label "redwood/gang=true" and gpu.vram>8Gi. Fallback: if pack would blow our packing efficiency beyond X%, allow spread.

kai: sounds sane. Quick mitigation while plugin is written: increase lateBind window from 1s -> 8s for pods with gang=true and set topologySpreadConstraints to preferByZone: "preferAvoid" -> reduce strictness. That should give binder slightly more time to find colocated nodes.

leah: agree on mitigation. downside: transient delay for scheduling small jobs (a few seconds) and slight up in node fragmentation. cost-wise we simulated +3% capacity need for same throughput.

maria: can we also add an admission hook to set annotation pack.colocate=true for jobs launched by the batching service? Ops told me batch service launches tens of tiny pods instead of a single gang, that's part of the problem.

sam: yes, we can push that. Also recommending a short-term k8s daemon that monitors nvlink peer metrics and taints nodes if interconnect drops below threshold (taint: nvlink-low).

nora: ops-bot: created incident INC-2026-042 where we’ll track the mitigation steps and rollback criteria :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-042 created by nora. Severity: P2. Runbook link: https://internal/runbooks/gpu-fractional-gang

kai: next steps: (1) implement scheduler preference (PR target: today EOD), (2) enable lateBind window increase behind feature flag, (3) admission hook for batch service, (4) nvlink health taint daemon pilot in us-west2 only.

maria: thanks — I'll put the rollout plan in the incident doc and ping batch service owners.

leah: postmortem note: add an eval that measures inference latency variance when pods are distributed vs colocated. We should quantify the cost/latency tradeoff before final roll.

maria: sounds good. if anyone hits repeat evictions, ping #oncall and attach fractional_gang_ratio and node nvlink metrics.

kai: one more thing — consider adding a pack-aware binpacker that can trade a 2% packing loss for 20% less interconnect traffic. I'll draft perf numbers in PR.

maria: thanks all, closing thread but keeping incident open for now :white_check_mark:
